title: US government, Google join Zuckerberg-backed Biohub in $1.8 billion push for AI biology data
source_used: Reuters (original blocked here: HTTP 401); read through The American Bazaar, which states it is reporting Reuters, cross-checked with Türkiye Today (citing Biohub's statement)
key_facts: Biohub, the nonprofit founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Dr Priscilla Chan, is leading a $1.8 billion Virtual Biology Initiative to generate large biological datasets for AI.
The aim is data that can help AI systems predict how cells and biological systems respond to diseases, environmental conditions and treatments.
Google DeepMind, Meta and Isomorphic Labs (an AI drug discovery company) will together invest $300 million.
The US Department of Energy is committing more than $500 million over five years; the National Institutes of Health is coordinating federal participation and contributing datasets.
Biohub had earlier committed $500 million to the effort.
Biohub expects to release its first major dataset within a year and aims to have functional predictive models within five years, according to Reuters.
Investors will get an initial period of exclusive access to some data before it becomes an open resource for researchers.
quote_evidence: The initiative, known as the Virtual Biology Initiative, aims to generate data that can help AI systems predict how cells and biological systems respond to diseases, environmental conditions and potential treatments.
The resulting datasets are intended to become an open resource for researchers, although investors will receive an initial period of exclusive access to some data.
Biohub expects to release its first major dataset within a year and aims to have functional predictive models within five years.
why_it_matters_hint: Scientists could test biology digitally rather than only in labs, which could speed up drug research, though the datasets and models are still to be built.
notes: Reuters original blocked here (401), so the facts come from The American Bazaar's account of Reuters' report, which names Reuters as the source; Türkiye Today gives the same funding split from Biohub's statement. Source credited as Reuters, relayed by The American Bazaar. Timelines are Reuters' stated targets.
